headline: Apple proposes up to 15% commission for off-App Store purchases
summary: Apple has submitted its proposal for fees on purchases made outside its App Store system in the ongoing Epic Games case.
details: Apple has proposed charging commissions of up to 15% for purchases made outside of its App Store. This proposal comes as part of the ongoing legal battle with Epic Games in the United States.

The tech giant's submission outlines the fees it believes are appropriate for transactions that bypass the traditional App Store payment system. This move is a direct response to court orders aimed at increasing competition.

Meanwhile, a judge has ordered Google to make it easier for users to install rival app stores on Android devices. This ruling is part of a separate but related legal challenge concerning Google's app store practices.
These developments signal a potential shift in how app stores operate and generate revenue, with regulators and courts pushing for more openness and competition in the digital marketplace.
